{{short description|On kernels of maps between abelianized fundamental groups of schemes and fields}}

In [[number theory]], the '''Katz–Lang finiteness theorem''', proved by {{harvs|txt|first1=Nick|last1=Katz|author1-link=Nick Katz|last2=Lang|first2=Serge|author2-link=Serge Lang|year=1981}}, states that if ''X'' is a [[smooth scheme|smooth]], [[geometrically (algebraic geometry)|geometrically]] connected [[Scheme (mathematics)|scheme]] of [[scheme of finite type|finite type]] over a [[field (mathematics)|field]] ''K'' that is finitely generated over the [[prime field]], and Ker(''X''/''K'') is the kernel of the maps between their [[abelianization|abelianized]] [[fundamental group]]s, then Ker(''X''/''K'') is finite if ''K'' has characteristic 0, and the part of the kernel coprime to ''p'' is finite if ''K'' has characteristic ''p''&nbsp;>&nbsp;0.
